messages:
maria (seceng): heads-up: we're getting a big spike of 'suspicious-command-exec' alerts since 15:22. dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/alerts?view=cmd-exec - looks noisy, likely FP but want confirmation before muting
AlertBot: [AUTOMATION] Rule 'suspicious-command-exec' (id: R-9821) fired 124 times in 10m across 46 hosts. Severity: medium. Link: https://siem.internal/alerts/R-9821/1745216789
aj (infra): I can see a lot of those events coming from backup cluster nodes (10.21.x.x). They all report user=backup-svc and process=/usr/local/bin/backup-runner
sam (sre): can you paste a few raw events? want to be sure it's the same command string each time
maria (seceng): here's a quick export (KQL) and sample lines:
```
index=logs-* | where rule_id=="R-9821" | project host, user, process, command, timestamp | sort by timestamp desc | limit 10
host: backup-03, user: backup-svc, process: /usr/local/bin/backup-runner, command: "curl -s http://internal-metrics/metrics | sh", ts: 2025-06-18T15:20:10Z
host: backup-04, user: backup-svc, process: /usr/local/bin/backup-runner, command: "curl -s http://internal-metrics/metrics | sh", ts: 2025-06-18T15:20:11Z
...
```
oliver (devex): that pattern explains it. internal maintenance task curling an internal endpoint and piping to sh — annoying but expected for the backup runner. we should tune the rule rather than silence it globally
natalie (prodsec): options: 1) add an allowlist for user=="backup-svc" and process=="/usr/local/bin/backup-runner" with justification 2) add a suppression window for identical command from same service 3) require more distributed indicators (e.g., >3 unique user accounts or >5 distinct host namespaces)
sam (sre): i prefer adding a condition to the detection: require distinct_source_count > 3 or command not in allowlist. otherwise single-service noise will keep firing. example change (pseudo-KQL):
```
from logs where command matches /curl .*metrics/ and NOT (user=="backup-svc" and process=="/usr/local/bin/backup-runner") and distinct_count(host) > 3 within 60s
```
mike (oncall): can someone push a temp suppress to reduce paging? set mute on rule R-9821 for 30m and post the change in the pagerduty note. will escalate if we see real deviation
maria (seceng): i'll apply a staging-rule tweak now to exclude backup-svc and add a distinct_host threshold. will run it in staging for 15m then promote. jira: RDW-3912 created to track permanent rule update and playbook edits: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RDW-3912
aj (infra): aside: we should enrich events with svc_account tag at ingest (CI already annotates pods). that way future rules can easily filter internal services without fragile command regexes
oliver (devex): also add a dashboard panel for 'rule false positive ratio' using manual tagging (fp / total) so we can see tuning impact after changes
natalie (prodsec): post-incident actions: - update alert runbook with allowlist criteria and owner - create scheduled job to review top-10 noisy rules monthly - add automated annotation when we add an allowlist entry (who/why)
sam (sre): i've applied mute in PD and marked this alert as 'investigating -> noise' on the SIEM side. will collect metrics during the 30m window and report back
mike (oncall): thanks. once staging looks good, promote to prod and include runbook link in alert message. PV: reduce pages for known maintenance jobs
maria (seceng): agreed. i'll follow up with PR to rules repo and add the runbook link to R-9821. tagging ticket RDW-3912 and adding owners @aj @sam for rollout. resolving thread for now :thumbsup:
